name: ALLWIN
author: strings-agent
description: HARD. De Bruijn sequence B(k,n). Clue is 'ALPHABET N', e.g. 'ab 4' or 'abc 3'. Solution: a cyclic string of length len(ALPHABET)**N over that alphabet in which every one of the k**n windows of length N occurs exactly once (wrapping around the end). Scorer: length check, alphabet check, and 'the k**n rotated windows are all distinct' (~155 chars) - trivial to verify, genuinely hard to find. Solve: the standard FKM / Lyndon-word algorithm, ~0.4 ms for the largest case (256 chars). Discovery path: the clue is two tiny fields; a demo gives a 16-character a/b string for 'ab 4', and len == 2**4 is the first thing anyone notices. From there the AI teammate is very likely to recognise a de Bruijn sequence. Hardest of my six and deliberately all-or-nothing: there is no partial credit, but the easiest instances (ab 3, abc 2) are small enough to find by random search / backtracking, which is the ramp.
